text: A four-hop payment cycle moved $70.01 out of accounts linked to broker Eric Maynard and Johnson Medical Centre, through two unowned shell accounts, and back over 53 days, returning $47.13 - 32.7% attrition. The amount is small, but the structure is the point: closed loops through shells are the plumbing of kickback recycling, and this loop connects the same broker-clinic pair already flagged for referral concentration. Each hop shows the drip-fee pattern of conduit accounts rather than any recognizable commercial payment. The honest alternative is a chain of small service fees that happens to close a circle, which whole-ledger review can rule in or out. Next step: pull the complete inbound and outbound history of the two shell accounts - a conduit used once is an anecdote, a conduit used repeatedly is infrastructure.
